disposition_mapping.rationale: Extraction and closing-rate retranslation remain mandatory and inseparable (KB-07), but the mechanism is restructured to support two first-class, equally compliant execution modes — automated connector and manual/batch upload — rather than assuming universal connectivity. The GL accountant's role shifts from manual pulling to completeness validation and exception triage on an exception worklist, with extraction failures and stale-rate conditions surfaced rather than silently logged. The reconciliation schedule by risk rating and closing exchange rates remain hard, unconditional inputs (ACR-R-01, ACR-R-07), satisfying both the standards requirement and the infrastructure-equity concern raised across the council.

Matching is kept as its own named step, distinct from extraction, rather than fused into a single pipeline step — matching-rule logic and retranslation methodology are differently governed artifacts (KB-06) and keeping them separately auditable preserves the ability to pinpoint which governed artifact changed when outcomes drift. The function is restructured toward heavier automation of the matched population, but the exception queue — now carrying match-rule provenance and exception-type tags for FX and intercompany breaks — is the real deliverable, satisfying KB-08 and KB-14 traceability. Manual matching remains a compliant mode where comparison data quality does not support automation, so the requirement that matching 'survive in some form' is honored as a genuine, visible control point with a named actor, not dissolved into background infrastructure.

Investigation and classification remain irreducibly human-led judgment work (KB-02, KB-05) and are not shrunk to population-exception triage of 'only novel items' — the council's deskilling concern is taken seriously. The restructuring adds suggest-only AI assistance with mandatory, logged accept/override, and makes the mechanical-versus-estimation distinction explicit at this step so estimation items are correctly routed downstream, but final accountability and effort remain with the GL accountant across the full unmatched population.

Adjusting entry preparation remains distinct from investigation and from reviewer approval, continues to consume the prior-period error record for retrospective correction (ACR-R-06, KB-05), and now explicitly absorbs preparer sign-off's function. Mechanical entries may be system-drafted; estimation-based entries (NRV write-downs, ECL-type provisions, judgment accruals) retain a named accountable human preparer with a documented basis per KB-04/KB-10. This is where the council's convergence (finance_domain, hitl_designer, agentic_architect, and accounting_standards on standards-sufficiency grounds) lands: preparation and attestation are one transaction performed by one accountable actor, not two artificially separated handoffs.

Marked unconstrained by design, and the council's majority (hitl_designer, finance_domain, agentic_architect, pragmatist on reconsideration, accounting_standards on standards-sufficiency grounds) converged on merging sign-off into adjusting-entry preparation rather than eliminating it outright as maximalist proposed. The synthesis rejects elimination: a system activity log proving a JE was created is not the same artifact as a captured human assertion of completeness and correctness (KB-02's evidential trail is strongest with an explicit claim, not inferred activity). The merge is accepted on the condition — carried into TS-04's definition — that the attestation artifact (preparer identity, timestamp, explicit completeness confirmation) survives as a distinct named output, addressing pragmatist's, hitl_designer's and accounting_standards' shared insistence that the accountability record must not vanish along with the step boundary.

Independent reviewer approval is the one control every council member treated as non-negotiable, and the synthesis holds it exactly there: a structurally distinct actor from the TS-04 preparer (ACR-R-05), reviewing every reconciliation rather than a rule-engine auto-approving a risk tier. Finance_domain's proposal for threshold-based auto-certification of zero-variance accounts is rejected — pragmatist, accounting_standards and agentic_architect converge against it, since a 'zero-variance' classification is itself a system judgment requiring an external check. Risk-tiering is accepted only as attention allocation (deeper scrutiny where warranted, periodic sampling elsewhere), never as removal of the human gate, and the reviewer is fed exception-level detail rather than totals, per hitl_designer's and accounting_standards' shared refinement.

The synthesis rejects both full automation of the escalation decision (agentic_architect's original SLA-failure-backstop design, maximalist's absorption into reviewer approval) and resistance to automating detection. Detection is automated and continuous, run as a portfolio-level, cross-entity surveillance function per finance_domain's and hitl_designer's convergent argument — per-account review cannot see the pattern of an item 'explained' identically for six periods. The escalation decision itself remains a controller-led human judgment made at first breach, reflecting the round-two convergence of hitl_designer, finance_domain, pragmatist, accounting_standards and agentic_architect's own concession, against the minority SLA-failure-backstop design.

Evidence retention and status reporting survive as an explicit step with named outputs, not an implicit system byproduct, per the near-universal insistence (pragmatist, accounting_standards, emerging_economy, hitl_designer) that auditors ask for this artifact by name. The restructuring automates routine archival and aggregation while requiring a human completeness review of the status report before finalization, and explicitly names both immutable WORM-class archival and local/low-bandwidth storage with periodic sync and integrity checks as equally compliant retention mechanisms, resolving the conflict between agentic_architect's WORM-only design and emerging_economy's infrastructure-equity requirement in favor of plural, named compliant paths.

steps.actor: GL accountant (extraction exception handler, supported by automated extraction where infrastructure and data quality allow)
steps.description: GL and comparison balances are extracted for every in-scope account due under its risk-rated frequency via either an automated connector path or a manual/batch upload path (CSV, scanned statement, portal export) — both are first-class, equally compliant modes, not a primary path with a degraded fallback. Foreign-currency monetary balances are retranslated at the closing rate as an inseparable part of this step, not a downstream catch-up computation. Extraction failures, stale or missing rates, and accounts that failed to extract against the risk-rated schedule are surfaced to the GL accountant as a prioritized worklist, not buried in a system log.
inputs: Reconciliation schedule by account risk rating
steps.name: Automated/manual extraction, retranslation and exception flagging

steps.description: Transactions are matched between GL and comparison source: automatically via a versioned, change-logged rules engine (plus statistical assistance on the residual tail) where data quality and connectivity support it, and manually by the GL accountant where they do not — both modes are compliant and named explicitly. Unmatched and low-confidence items are routed to an exception queue that carries match-rule provenance (why an item didn't match, which rule nearly fired) and an exception-type tag (FX difference, intercompany break, timing difference, true error) captured at the point of queueing, so neither exchange differences nor intercompany breaks are netted invisibly or rediscovered later. Changes to matching tolerances or auto-match thresholds are treated as governed computation-method changes requiring policy-consistency review before deployment, not silent configuration edits.
steps.name: Transaction matching with provenance-carrying exception queue
outputs: Exception queue with provenance and type tags

steps.description: Unmatched items are investigated, explained, supported with evidence and classified by the GL accountant, who remains the sole accountable party for the final classification. A system may pre-draft a likely root cause and classification from historical resolution patterns, but this is suggest-only authority: every acceptance or override is an explicit, reasoned, logged human action, not a default confirm. Classification distinguishes mechanical corrections from estimation-based items (e.g. NRV write-downs, ECL-type provisions), routing the latter to the accountable-preparer path in adjusting entry preparation.
inputs: Exception queue with provenance and type tags
steps.name: Investigate, classify and resolve reconciling items

steps.description: Adjusting journal entries are prepared for items requiring correction, with prior-period errors corrected retrospectively using the prior-period error record, never absorbed as current-period noise. Mechanical, rule-based entries (reclasses, timing corrections, routine FX reval true-ups) may be system-drafted for preparer confirmation; estimation-based entries (provisions, NRV write-downs, ECL-type adjustments) require a named, accountable human preparer with a documented basis attached to the entry — no auto-posting of estimates. The preparer's completion attestation (identity, timestamp, explicit confirmation that the reconciliation and entries are complete and correct) is captured as a distinct, named output at the moment of finalization, in the same transaction as preparation, rather than as a separate later click reviewed with stale memory.
steps.name: Prepare and attest adjusting journal entries

steps.description: An independent reviewer, structurally and by identity distinct from the TS-04 preparer, reviews and approves the reconciliation and its adjusting entries. Every reconciliation passes through this mandatory human gate; review effort is risk-tiered by attention allocation — deeper scrutiny on estimates, overrides, FX and intercompany items, and aged carry-forwards, with periodic human sampling even on low-risk, fully-matched accounts — but no account population is auto-approved by a rule engine with zero human touch. The reviewer is fed exception-level detail (what changed since last period, which entries are estimates versus mechanical, which matches were overridden, outstanding aged items), not a totals-only summary.
inputs: Prepared reconciliation (explained and classified items plus preparer attestation)
steps.name: Reviewer approval with exception-level dashboard

steps.description: Reconciling items beyond the ageing threshold are detected continuously and exhaustively across the whole book of reconciliations by automated monitoring, run as a cross-entity, cadence-driven surveillance function independent of any single account's approval cycle — this is the only way to catch the account that has been 'explained' identically for six consecutive periods, which per-account review cannot see. Severity assessment, routing and the decision to escalate remain a controller-led human judgment made at first breach, not delegated to automated close-out logic and not deferred to an SLA-failure backstop, because escalation is a risk judgment on business exposure, not a notification event.
inputs: Ageing data across the reconciliation portfolio
steps.name: Aged-item surveillance and escalation

steps.description: Reconciliation evidence — matching trail, supporting documents, preparer attestation, reviewer approval decisions and escalation history — is retained either via immutable (WORM-class) archival where infrastructure supports it, or via local/low-bandwidth-compatible storage with a defined sync cadence and integrity check where it does not; both are compliant retention mechanisms, not a primary path and a tolerated exception. Reconciliation status is reported on schedule or on demand, in live-dashboard or batch-export form. The GL accountant retains explicit accountability for reviewing the status report for completeness exceptions (accounts that failed to reconcile, missed the risk-rated frequency, or carry unresolved escalations) before it is treated as final.
